title: Commissioners who are officers or staff of an organization the City pays
question: Which members of City boards and commissions are listed as officers, directors or key employees of a City-paid organization, and does their body oversee the department that pays it?
finding: 2 seat holders in the listings are named on the tax return of a City-paid organization and name the same organization on their own Form 700; for 0 of them the body they sit on oversees a department that paid the organization $25,000 or more since fiscal 2019. 120 more holders share a full name with one person on such a return without that confirmation (11 where the body oversees a paying department); they are counted and not named.
how: Holder names from the listings and names on the tax returns (Part VII officers, directors, key employees and highest paid) of organizations the City paid $25,000 or more since fiscal 2019 are reduced to first and last name. A holder is matched only where that name is on the returns of exactly one such organization, and shown only where the member's Form 700 Schedule C, filed for a board or commission seat, names that organization. "Oversees" maps the body's name to departments with the mapping in the “sidedoors” analysis.
limits: Name match: the confirmation makes a wrong person unlikely but not impossible. Many seats require a member from a provider, union or community group, and holding one is permitted; what matters is recusal from decisions about the organization, which the recusal notices (the site’s “Side doors: department gifts, commissioners, ballot committees, enforcement” page) and minutes would show. Payments are by department, not by decision of the body. Board seats of nonprofits are often unpaid.

columns.t: Those departments paid the organization since FY2019
